xBRIEFInfo.author: overdeck/0.0.0
xBRIEFInfo.description: Plan for PAN-3138: Merge-time Docker cleanup leaves workspace devnet behind — leaked subnets exhaust Docker address pools and block new workspaces

plan.title: Merge-time Docker cleanup leaves workspace devnet behind — leaked subnets exhaust Docker address pools and block new workspaces
plan.author: agent:k3[1m]

narratives.Problem: postMergeLifecycle (src/lib/cloister/merge-agent.ts:533-550) only stops workspace Docker containers; it never removes the workspace `_devnet` network. teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise (src/lib/workspace-manager/docker.ts:156) — the idempotent, name-based primitive that removes containers AND the network and disconnects shared sidecars like overdeck-traefik — is only called from close-out (src/lib/close-out.ts:365) and the closed-issue reaper (src/lib/cloister/reap-issue-residue.ts:50, tracker-closed issues only). Every merged issue therefore leaks its _devnet subnet (~31 usable in Docker's default pools) until close-out, which can lag merge by days; on 2026-07-26 five merged-but-not-closed issues exhausted the pool and blocked PAN-3093 workspace prep with 'all predefined address pools have been fully subnetted'.
narratives.Proposal: Three surgical changes on the existing verified teardown primitive, plus docs: (1) postMergeLifecycle calls teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise(issueLower) at merge time — unconditionally (name-based, works when the workspace dir is gone) and non-fatally; (2) the deacon's reconcileClosedIssueAgents devnet loop treats mergeStatus==='merged' (read via getReviewStatusSync, dynamic import) as Docker-teardown-eligible — network teardown only, no agent kills, no disk/branch reap; (3) rebuildWorkspaceStack treats mergeStatus==='merged' as terminal so patrols cannot recreate a torn-down network before close-out (aligns code with the invariant CLAUDE.md already documents). Full before/after snippets, decisions D1-D4, and hazards H1-H5 are in the PRD at .pan/drafts/PAN-3138.md.
narratives.NonGoals:
- No live pool-fill repro test (destructive to the host; AC3 is met with mocked-Docker unit regression tests — decision D2)
- No changes to teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise itself — it is already correct, idempotent, and tested
- No changes to close-out's teardown ownership or the full reapIssueResidue path for closed issues
- No tracker-API-based merged detection in the patrol (local review-status door only)
- No rework of Docker default-address-pool sizing or pan doctor thresholds (already covered by PAN-3053)

autoDecisions.summary: Implement both issue-proposed fixes (merge-time call + reaper backstop) instead of either/or
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue says 'alternatively/additionally'; the merge-time call is the root fix and the reaper extension is the straggler backstop, matching the repo's reaper-as-backstop doctrine.

autoDecisions.summary: Satisfy issue AC3 with mocked-Docker unit regression tests, not a scripted live pool-fill repro
autoDecisions.rationale: Filling the host's real Docker address pool is destructive to concurrent workspaces and not CI-safe; the leak was already demonstrated live in the issue, and the regression surface is that both call sites invoke the verified teardown primitive.

autoDecisions.summary: Read merged eligibility from getReviewStatusSync via dynamic import
autoDecisions.rationale: Avoids per-patrol tracker API calls and any static import cycle with review-status.js.

autoDecisions.summary: Add the rebuildWorkspaceStack merged-gate hardening (work item 3) beyond the issue's literal ask
autoDecisions.rationale: CLAUDE.md already claims the rebuild chokepoint no-ops for merged issues but the code only checks tracker-closed; without it a patrol can recreate a network the merge-time teardown just removed. Small, same-guard change; reopen clears mergeStatus.

items.title: postMergeLifecycle removes the workspace _devnet at merge time

expected_outputs: postmerge-cleanup-async.test.ts passes including the new teardown assertions

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cloister/merge-agent.ts step 4 (the Docker cleanup block at lines 533-550), keep the existing stopWorkspaceDocker behavior and ADD a call to teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise(issueLower) via dynamic import from '../workspace-manager/docker.js'. The call MUST be outside the `if (workspacePath)` gate (the primitive is name-based precisely for the workspace-dir-gone case), inside the existing try/catch so failures stay non-fatal (console.warn only; _completedPostMerge must still mark). When teardown.networkRemoved is true, console.log and logActivity('docker_cleanup', ...) the steps, matching the existing logging style. Use the exact before/after shape in the PRD (.pan/drafts/PAN-3138.md, 'Before / after — merge-agent.ts'). Then extend tests/unit/lib/cloister/postmerge-cleanup-async.test.ts: add vi.mock('../../../../src/lib/workspace-manager/docker.js', ...) exposing a teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise spy resolving { networkRemoved: true, steps: ['Removed network'] }; assert it is called with issueId.toLowerCase() (the file's fs.existsSync mock returns false, so this also proves the call is not gated on the workspace dir); add a case where the spy rejects and assert postMergeLifecycle still resolves and still calls mockSetAgentPaused and mockCreateResetMarker. Do not modify teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise or stopWorkspaceDocker.

items.title: Given a merged issue, when postMergeLifecycle completes, then it calls teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise with the lowercase issue id even when the workspace directory does not exist
Given the teardown call rejects, when postMergeLifecycle runs, then it resolves normally, still pauses agents and creates the memory reset marker, and logs a non-fatal warning
Given the existing stopWorkspaceDocker block, when the diff is reviewed, then it is preserved unchanged and the new teardown call appears after it, outside the `if (workspacePath)` gate
Deacon reaper tears down devnets of merged-but-not-closed issues (Docker only)

expected_outputs: closed-issue-reaper.test.ts passes including the new merged-issue cases

narrative.Action: In src/lib/cloister/closed-issue-reaper.ts, rework the devnet loop in reconcileClosedIssueAgents (currently lines 224-227): keep the closed-issue path exactly as-is (isClosedIssue → reapResolvedIssueResidue), and add an else branch for not-closed issues that dynamically imports getReviewStatusSync from '../review-status.js' and, when getReviewStatusSync(issueId)?.mergeStatus === 'merged', dynamically imports teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise from '../workspace-manager/docker.js' and calls it with issueId.toLowerCase(). Push a descriptive action string for the removed/still-present/failed outcomes, matching the PRD snippet ('Before / after — closed-issue-reaper.ts'). NEVER call reapIssueResidue, stopAgent, or any tmux/disk/branch step for merged-but-not-closed issues — Docker-network teardown only. No project resolution is needed (teardown is name-based). Wrap the merged branch in try/catch that pushes a failure action string instead of throwing. Then extend src/lib/cloister/__tests__/closed-issue-reaper.test.ts: add vi.mock for '../../review-status.js' (getReviewStatusSync) and '../../workspace-manager/docker.js' (teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise), and add cases: (a) leaked overdeck-feature-pan-5559_devnet + not tracker-closed + mergeStatus 'merged' → teardown called with 'pan-5559', reapIssueResidue NOT called, stopAgent NOT called, actions include the removal message; (b) same devnet + getReviewStatusSync returns null → teardown NOT called, actions empty; (c) existing test 'reaps closed-issue residue discovered from leaked _devnet networks' still passes unchanged.

items.title: Given a leaked _devnet whose issue is merged but not tracker-closed, when reconcileClosedIssueAgents runs, then it calls teardownWorkspaceDockerByNamePromise with the lowercase issue id and records a removal action
Given the same merged-issue devnet, when the patrol runs, then it does NOT call reapIssueResidue, does NOT call stopAgent, and does NOT touch the workspace dir or branch
Given a leaked devnet whose issue has no review-status row, when the patrol runs, then it skips the issue entirely and returns no actions for it
Given a leaked devnet whose issue is tracker-closed, when the patrol runs, then the full reapIssueResidue path still fires exactly as before this change

expected_outputs: rebuild-stack.test.ts passes including the new merged-gate cases

narrative.Action: In src/lib/workspace/rebuild-stack.ts, extend the terminal guard inside Effect.gen (currently lines 166-173): in addition to the existing isIssueClosed check, dynamically import getReviewStatusSync from '../review-status.js' and treat getReviewStatusSync(issueId)?.mergeStatus === 'merged' as terminal, returning the same { success: false, error: 'Issue is terminal (closed/merged) — skipping stack rebuild' } shape. Use the PRD snippet ('Before / after — rebuild-stack.ts'). This aligns the code with the invariant the workspace CLAUDE.md already documents ('rebuildWorkspaceStack no-ops for closed/merged issues'); isIssueClosed alone only covers tracker-closed. Reopen clears mergeStatus, so reopened issues rebuild normally. Then extend src/lib/workspace/__tests__/rebuild-stack.test.ts in the 'rebuildWorkspaceStack terminal-state guard (PAN-2510)' describe: add vi.mock for '../../review-status.js'; new cases: (a) isIssueClosed false + mergeStatus 'merged' → result.error contains 'terminal' and no rebuild proceeds; (b) isIssueClosed false + mergeStatus undefined or 'failed' → proceeds past the guard (same assertion style as the existing 'proceeds past the guard' test).

items.title: Given an issue with mergeStatus 'merged' that is not tracker-closed, when rebuildWorkspaceStack runs, then it returns the terminal error and performs no compose down/render/up steps
Given an issue with mergeStatus unset or 'failed' that is not tracker-closed, when rebuildWorkspaceStack runs, then it proceeds past the terminal guard exactly as before this change
Document merge-time Docker teardown ownership in WORKSPACE-CONTAINERS.md and CLAUDE.md

expected_outputs: Both docs state that merge removes the workspace containers AND the _devnet network, with close-out as durable verified owner and the reaper as merged-issue backstop

narrative.Action: Update two doc surfaces to match the new behavior. (1) docs/WORKSPACE-CONTAINERS.md, the teardown-ownership section near line 115 ('Close-out is the durable owner.'): add that postMergeLifecycle now removes the workspace Docker stack AND the overdeck-feature-<issue>_devnet network eagerly at merge time via the same name-based teardown, that close-out remains the durable verified owner, and that the deacon's reaper patrol also tears down devnets of merged-but-not-closed issues as a backstop. (2) Workspace CLAUDE.md, section 'postMergeLifecycle Verify Handoff and Docker Cleanup': change the sentence that says merge 'stops Docker containers and networks' to state that merge-time cleanup now REMOVES containers and the _devnet network (not just stops containers), and that the rebuildWorkspaceStack chokepoint no-ops for closed AND merged issues (it already claims this — the code now matches). Keep the existing 'NEVER remove this cleanup step' warning and the Docker-pool rationale intact. Do not rewrite surrounding sections.

items.title: Given the merged implementation, when a reviewer reads docs/WORKSPACE-CONTAINERS.md, then its teardown-ownership section contains the statement that postMergeLifecycle removes the workspace stack and _devnet at merge time and preserves the close-out durable-owner and reaper-backstop roles

CLAUDE.md's 'postMergeLifecycle Verify Handoff and Docker Cleanup' section states that merge removes containers AND the network and that rebuildWorkspaceStack no-ops for closed and merged issues, and preserves the existing NEVER-remove warning
